title: Behavioral Equivalence Cannot See Dormant Logic: A Pre-Registered Negative Result from a Five-Arm Comparison of PLC Command Gates on a Simulated PLC
description: WACE Technical Report TR-2026-01, version 1.3 (revised 2026-09-25; v1.0 released 2026-09-21). v1.3 changes only the author's name to its passport spelling, Dong Gul Bang (v1.0–v1.2: Dongkeol Bang); no text or number changes (Errata E6). v1.2 corrects an overstatement, present since v1.0, about what is public: the result files, row labels and pre-registration are held by the company and are not public (Errata E5); no number changes. Defensive publication. A pre-registered five-arm comparison of PLC command gates on a simulated PLC: adding a behavioral-equivalence check did not change what the gate lets through (23 of 280 hazardous false passes in both arms before a design revision; 19 of 278 in both arms, identical on every verdict count, after it). The four person-exposure false passes that remain are writes made while a timer preset had been changed in the plant program only — a dormant program difference that no observation-based check sees; a static program-signature check must precede any behavioral check, and on protocols without a program signature (Modbus) the gate cannot see this class of change. v1.1 corrects two factual errors of v1.0: four false passes that v1.0 attributed to a removed interlock were commands issued while the PLC was halted (now refused by a scan-counter heartbeat), and v1.0's prediction that the other four would close by rewriting two rules was wrong. See ERRATA.md. Results are from a simulated PLC on one machine; no physical PLC comparison is included. The report publishes its run ledger, denominators and excluded rows, and states its known limitations.
